title: Lester's perfect ear and learning Louis Armstrong's solos
summary: Lester learned Armstrong solos after hearing them once and taught the others parts by note without chord names.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Did you work on any arrangements from Louis' records?
No. We never bothered on Louis' too much. Louis... I don't know. Mostly singing and a solo, too, you
know. The only thing... We just listened to him play the horn.
Did Lester ever learn any of his solos?
Did he ever learn them so he could play them?

Yeah. All he'd do was listen to them once. He had that kind of ear, man. That cat had a perfect ear. We used to go to the record store maybe a month later. He'd say, "Hey, Deak!" "Yeah?" "Do you remember this?" He'd play it, and I'd forgot what it was. Someplace where we listened to records. And he'd play it. I'd say, "Yeah, man." He'd say, "We gon' learn that." So we'd get together, you know... Because we all...easy to pick up. You know, I was easy to pick up and Pete was easy to pick up.
Easy to pick up, you mean easy to...?

Pick up what he gave us. Yeah. See, he was just a born genius, man. I mean, he was a born musician. Now, he didn't know what note... He wouldn't say, "Man, you play D-flat or you play so-and-so," breaking the chord in two, what you call... He'd just say, "You play this note here," and he'd make it on his horn, "and you play this note." Then we'd hit it. Well, I'd tell him "that's my so-and-so." Well, he'd say "That's the note I want you to play." Then we'd play
that, and then we'd run it down. It would be real pretty.
